title: Noetherian approximation of a finitely presented algebra and module (Stacks 00R1)
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and let $M$ be a finitely presented $S$-module, meaning that $M$ is the cokernel of an $S$-linear map $S^{\oplus a}\to S^{\oplus b}$ for finite $a,b$. Then there are a nonempty directed set $(\Lambda,\le)$, ring maps $R_\lambda\to S_\lambda$ and $S_\lambda$-modules $M_\lambda$ for $\lambda\in\Lambda$, compatible transition maps and maps to $R,S,M$, such that: (1) $R=\varinjlim R_\lambda$, $S=\varinjlim S_\lambda$ as rings and $M=\varinjlim M_\lambda$ as abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], compatibly with $R\to S$ and the module actions; (2) each $R_\lambda$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and each $S_\lambda$ is of finite type over $R_\lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], while $M_\lambda$ is finitely generated over $S_\lambda$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; (3) for every $\lambda\le\mu$, the canonical maps $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\to S_\mu$ and $M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S_\mu\to M_\mu$ are isomorphisms; (4) for every $\lambda$, the canonical maps $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R\to S$ and $M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S\to M$ are isomorphisms, so also $M_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R\to M$ is an isomorphism of $R$-modules.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00R1 (lemma-limit-module-finite-presentation), lines 32593-32625, including the displayed 'in particular' isomorphisms

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-finite-presentation] (Stacks 00R0) to the finitely presented ring map $\varphi:R\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. It gives a nonempty directed set $(\Lambda,\le)$, ring maps $\rho_\lambda:R_\lambda\to S_\lambda$, transition ring maps $r_{\mu\lambda}:R_\lambda\to R_\mu$, $s_{\mu\lambda}:S_\lambda\to S_\mu$ ($\lambda\le\mu$) compatible with the $\rho$'s, and ring maps $\pi_\lambda:R_\lambda\to R$, $\kappa_\lambda:S_\lambda\to S$ with $\varphi\pi_\lambda=\kappa_\lambda\rho_\lambda$, such that $(R,(\pi_\lambda))$ and $(S,(\kappa_\lambda))$ are colimits of the systems $(R_\lambda)$, $(S_\lambda)$ in commutative rings, $R_\lambda$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, $S_\lambda$ is of finite type over $R_\lambda$, $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\to S_\mu$ is an isomorphism for $\lambda\le\mu$, and $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R\to S$, $s\otimes r\mapsto\kappa_\lambda(s)\varphi(r)$, is an isomorphism for every $\lambda$. This is the first sentence of the proof of 00QX ('write $R=\operatorname{colim}R_\lambda$ ... $S=\operatorname{colim}S_\lambda$'), in its non-local form.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00QX (lemma-limit-module-essentially-finite-presentation), proof, first two sentences ('As in the proof of Lemma 00QV we may first write R = colim R_lambda ... S = colim S_lambda'), non-local version 00R0

proof.text: Choose a presentation of $M$: an $S$-linear map $u:S^{\oplus a}\to S^{\oplus b}$ with cokernel $q:S^{\oplus b}\to M$, and let $(u_{kl})\in\operatorname{Mat}(b\times a,S)$ be its matrix ($u(e_l)=\sum_ku_{kl}e_k$). By clause (1) of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], applied to the directed set $\Lambda$ (a small filtered category) and the colimit $(S,(\kappa_\lambda))$ of step 1, each of the finitely many entries $u_{kl}$ is $\kappa_{\lambda_{kl}}(x_{kl})$ for some $\lambda_{kl}\in\Lambda$ and $x_{kl}\in S_{\lambda_{kl}}$. Since $\Lambda$ is nonempty and directed, there is $\lambda_0\in\Lambda$ with $\lambda_0\ge\lambda_{kl}$ for all $k,l$ (any $\lambda_0$ if $ab=0$); put $u_{\lambda_0,kl}=s_{\lambda_0\lambda_{kl}}(x_{kl})\in S_{\lambda_0}$. Then $\kappa_{\lambda_0}(u_{\lambda_0,kl})=u_{kl}$ for all $k,l$, because $\kappa_{\lambda_0}s_{\lambda_0\lambda_{kl}}=\kappa_{\lambda_{kl}}$. For $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$ let $u_\lambda:S_\lambda^{\oplus a}\to S_\lambda^{\oplus b}$ be the $S_\lambda$-linear map with matrix $(s_{\lambda\lambda_0}(u_{\lambda_0,kl}))$; then $s_{\mu\lambda}$ applied entrywise carries the matrix of $u_\lambda$ to that of $u_\mu$ ($\lambda_0\le\lambda\le\mu$), and $\kappa_\lambda$ carries it to $(u_{kl})$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00QX (lemma-limit-module-essentially-finite-presentation), proof, 'Choose a presentation S^s -> S^t -> M -> 0 ... we can find a matrix A_{lambda_2} in Mat(t x s, S_{lambda_2}) which maps to A'

proof.text: Put $\Lambda_0=\{\lambda\in\Lambda:\lambda\ge\lambda_0\}$. It is nonempty ($\lambda_0\in\Lambda_0$) and directed (an upper bound in $\Lambda$ of $\lambda,\lambda'\in\Lambda_0$ is $\ge\lambda_0$), and every $\lambda\in\Lambda$ has some $\mu\in\Lambda_0$ with $\lambda\le\mu$ (an upper bound of $\lambda,\lambda_0$). Regard $\Lambda$ as a category with a morphism $\lambda\to\mu$ iff $\lambda\le\mu$; then $\mathcal I=\Lambda^{\mathrm{op}}$ is cofiltered and its full subcategory $\mathcal J=\Lambda_0^{\mathrm{op}}$ satisfies the hypothesis of clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory] (every object $\lambda$ of $\mathcal I$ receives the morphism $\mu\to\lambda$ of $\mathcal I$ from the $\mu\in\Lambda_0$ just found). That clause, applied to the systems $(R_\lambda)$ and $(S_\lambda)$ in commutative rings, shows that $(R,(\pi_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_0})$ and $(S,(\kappa_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_0})$ are still colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the restricted systems over $\Lambda_0$. The other properties of step 1 hold for all $\lambda\le\mu$ in $\Lambda_0$, being properties of single indices or pairs. From now on the index set is $\Lambda_0$; this gives the ring part of clauses (1)-(4) of the statement: (2) and the ring isomorphisms of (3) and (4) are those of step 1.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00QX (lemma-limit-module-essentially-finite-presentation), proof, 'For all lambda >= lambda_2 we let M_lambda = Coker(S_lambda^s --A_lambda--> S_lambda^t)'

proof.text: Base change of the cokernels. Let $\sigma:S_\lambda\to T$ be either $s_{\mu\lambda}:S_\lambda\to S_\mu$ ($\lambda\le\mu$ in $\Lambda_0$, $T=S_\mu$, $u_T=u_\mu$, $q_T=q_\mu$) or $\kappa_\lambda:S_\lambda\to S$ ($T=S$, $u_T=u$, $q_T=q$); in both cases $\sigma$ carries the matrix of $u_\lambda$ to that of $u_T$ (step 2). By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], tensoring the exact sequence $S_\lambda^{\oplus a}\xrightarrow{u_\lambda}S_\lambda^{\oplus b}\xrightarrow{q_\lambda}M_\lambda\to0$ with $T$ over $S_\lambda$ gives an exact sequence $S_\lambda^{\oplus a}\otimes_{S_\lambda}T\to S_\lambda^{\oplus b}\otimes_{S_\lambda}T\to M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}T\to0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product] (with all $P_k=S_\lambda$, $N=T$) followed by the isomorphism $S_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}T\to T$, $y\otimes t\mapsto\sigma(y)t$, in each coordinate, $\theta_n:S_\lambda^{\oplus n}\otimes_{S_\lambda}T\xrightarrow{\sim}T^{\oplus n}$, $(y_k)\otimes t\mapsto(\sigma(y_k)t)$, an isomorphism which is $T$-linear (check on generators). On generators $e_l\otimes1$ one computes $\theta_b((u_\lambda\otimes1)(e_l\otimes1))=\sum_k\sigma(u_{\lambda,kl})e_k=u_T(e_l)=u_T(\theta_a(e_l\otimes1))$, so $\theta_b(u_\lambda\otimes1)=u_T\theta_a$ ($T$-linear maps agreeing on generators). Hence $M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}T\cong\operatorname{coker}(u_\lambda\otimes1)\cong\operatorname{coker}(u_T)$, and the resulting $T$-linear isomorphism $M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}T\to\operatorname{coker}(u_T)$ is $q_\lambda(y)\otimes t\mapsto t\,q_T(\sigma(y))$. For $T=S_\mu$ this is $x\otimes t\mapsto t\,n_{\mu\lambda}(x)$, $M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S_\mu\xrightarrow{\sim}M_\mu$ (module part of clause (3)); for $T=S$ it is $x\otimes t\mapsto t\,\nu_\lambda(x)$, $M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ (module part of clause (4)).

u_{\lambda_0}$ (step 4). Transporting along these bijections: every element of $M$ is $
u_\lambda(x)$ for some $\lambda\in\Lambda_0$, $x\in M_\lambda$, and $
u_\lambda(x)=0$ implies $n_{\mu\lambda}(x)=0$ for some $\mu\ge\lambda$. These are hypotheses (1), (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-criterion] for $\mathbf Z$-modules (abelian groups) and the cocone $(M,(
u_\lambda))$ (a cocone by step 4), which therefore is a colimit of $(M_\lambda,n_{\mu\lambda})_{\Lambda_0}$ in abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; the module actions are compatible by the semilinearity of the $

proof.text: The isomorphism $M_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R\cong M$ (end of clause (4); the 'in particular' $M=M_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R$ of 00R1). Fix $\lambda\in\Lambda_0$; $M_\lambda$ is an $R_\lambda$-module via $\rho_\lambda$ and $R$ an $R_\lambda$-algebra via $\pi_\lambda$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-cancel-base-change] (with $R\to S$ there being $\rho_\lambda:R_\lambda\to S_\lambda$, $M=M_\lambda$, $N=R$), $M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}(S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R)\cong M_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R$ via $x\otimes(y\otimes r)\mapsto yx\otimes r$, with inverse $x\otimes r\mapsto x\otimes(1\otimes r)$. Compose this inverse with $1\otimes\beta_\lambda$, where $\beta_\lambda:S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$, $y\otimes r\mapsto\kappa_\lambda(y)\varphi(r)$, is the ring isomorphism of step 1 (an isomorphism of $S_\lambda$-modules, so $1\otimes\beta_\lambda$ is an isomorphism), and then with the isomorphism $M_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S\to M$ of step 5. The composite $M_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R\to M$ is $x\otimes r\mapsto x\otimes(1\otimes r)\mapsto x\otimes\varphi(r)\mapsto\varphi(r)\nu_\lambda(x)$, a bijective $R$-linear map, i.e. an isomorphism of $R$-modules.

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Stacks 00R1 (algebra.tex lines 32593-32625): it matches, with the colimit of the M_lambda read as abelian groups compatible with the module actions, and the 'in particular' isomorphisms included as clause (4). Stacks proves 00R1 only by 'non-local version of 00QX, proof similar and left to the reader'; 00QX's proof is: take the ring system, descend the presentation matrix to a stage lambda_2, set M_lambda = coker(A_lambda) for lambda >= lambda_2, rest left to the reader. The split follows that proof: step 1 takes the ring system from the existing node for 00R0 (lem-weil-pbc-limit-finite-presentation, same unit), step 2 descends the matrix (elementwise colimit of rings), step 3 restricts to the cofinal Lambda_0 (cofinality node), step 4 defines M_lambda and the semilinear maps, step 5 proves both base-change isomorphisms by right exactness of tensor and S_lambda^n tensor T = T^n, step 6 proves M = colim M_lambda via the elementwise base-change colimit lemma and the colimit criterion for modules, step 7 the isomorphism M_lambda tensor_{R_lambda} R = M by tensor cancellation. No new node was needed: every fact used is an existing node (four of them Mathlib leaves). The suggested nodes lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-noetherian-approximation (global complete intersections), lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-essentially-finite-presentation-over-system (local rings, localization version) and lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-hom-directed-colimit (Hom of O_X-modules on schemes) do not state what the steps need and are not cited. No Lean on slopmaster2 states 00R1 (Algebra.FinitePresentation.exists_fg_subalgebra_isPushout in WeilConjectures/Mathlib/RingTheory/FinitePresentation.lean is the algebra part at one stage only, without the module or the directed system).

Steps 1-7 together realize the finite-presentation descent of an algebra and a module that this chain uses at that place; no step corresponds to a separate sentence of the blueprint proof.

Algebra.FiniteType (A.obj i) (B.obj i)) ∧ (∀ i, Module.Finite (B.obj i) (D.obj i)) ∧ -- (3) transition base changes (∀ (i j : Λ) (h : i ≤ j), letI := (η.app i).hom.toAlgebra letI := (A.map (homOfLE h)).hom.toAlgebra ∃ e : B.obj i ⊗[A.obj i] A.obj j ≃+* B.obj j, ∀ (x : B.obj i) (y : A.obj j), e (x ⊗ₜ[A.obj i] y) = (B.map (homOfLE h)).hom x * (η.app j).hom y) ∧ (∀ (i j : Λ) (h : i ≤ j), letI := (B.map (homOfLE h)).hom.toAlgebra ∃ e : B.obj j ⊗[B.obj i] D.obj i ≃ₗ[B.obj j] D.obj j, ∀ (y : B.obj j) (x : D.obj i), e (y ⊗ₜ[B.obj i] x) = y • (D.map (homOfLE h)).hom x) ∧ -- (4) base changes to the limit (∀ i, letI := (η.app i).hom.toAlgebra letI := (@CommRingCat.Hom.hom _ (CommRingCat.of R) (π.app i)).toAlgebra ∃ e : B.obj i ⊗[A.obj i] R ≃+* S, ∀ (x : B.obj i) (y : R), e (x ⊗ₜ[A.obj i] y) = (@CommRingCat.Hom.hom _ (CommRingCat.of S) (κ.app i)) x * algebraMap R S y) ∧ (∀ i, letI := (@CommRingCat.Hom.hom _ (CommRingCat.of S) (κ.app i)).toAlgebra ∃ e : S ⊗[B.obj i] D.obj i ≃ₗ[S] M, ∀ (y : S) (x : D.obj i), e (y ⊗ₜ[B.obj i] x) = y • (@AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom _ (AddCommGrpCat.of M) (ν.app i)) x) ∧ (∀ i, letI := (@CommRingCat.Hom.hom _ (CommRingCat.of R) (π.app i)).toAlgebra letI : Module (A.obj i) (D.obj i) := Module.compHom (D.obj i) (η.app i).hom letI : Module R M := Module.compHom M (algebraMap R S) ∃ e : R ⊗[A.obj i] D.obj i ≃ₗ[R] M, ∀ (y : R) (x : D.obj i), e (y ⊗ₜ[A.obj i] x) = algebraMap R S y • (@AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom _ (AddCommGrpCat.of M) (ν.app i)) x)
